canonical_title: The Shifting Realities of Philip K. Dick: Selected Literary and Philosophical Writings
author: Philip K. Dick (edited by Lawrence Sutin)
card_summary: Lawrence Sutin's 1995 edited collection of Dick's essays, speeches, and philosophical writings, the standard one-volume gathering of his nonfiction prose across three decades.
page_summary:
Edited by Lawrence Sutin and published in 1995, The Shifting Realities of Philip K. Dick collects the scattered nonfiction of a writer known mainly for his novels. It brings together essays, speeches, autobiographical statements, book introductions, and philosophical fragments, including major pieces such as "How to Build a Universe That Doesn't Fall Apart Two Days Later" and "The Android and the Human," arranged so a reader can trace the ideas that underlie the fiction.

The volume is the essential companion to Dick's novels for anyone interested in his thought rather than only his plots. Across some three hundred pages it documents his recurring questions, what is real, what is human, how authority manufactures false worlds, and how the self survives inside them, in his own discursive voice.

The portal preserves one archive manifestation. It complements the Exegesis materials by gathering the more finished, public-facing statements of the same preoccupations the notebooks pursue privately.
